Problem 2 Part(b)

```{r}
set.seed(1)

ar1 = arima.sim(model=list(order = c(7, 0, 0), ar = c(0.7, -0.7^2, 0.7^3, -0.7^4, 0.7^5, -0.7^6, 0.7^7)), n = 500)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 5.3, 2.1))
plot(ar1)
acf(ar1, lag.max = 20, ylim = c(-1, 1))
```
It is close to the ACF of the MA(1) model above. The above calculation shows that the model's ACF = 1 at h=0, and ACF = 79/149 = 0.4698 at h=1, and ACF = 0, at h>=2. From the ACF plot, at h=0 and h=1, the corresponding sample ACF's are approximatly 1 and 0.47. For h>=2, none of the sample ACFs is significant (all of them are within the blue dotted significance band), which is consistent to the model. 

Problem 3

Part(a)
```{r}
ts1 = ts(read.table("SUNSPOTS.txt"))

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 5.3, 2.1))
plot(ts1, ylab="SUNSPOTS", main="Time Plot of SUNSPOTS")
acf(ts1, lag.max = 99, ylim=c(-1,1), main="Correlogram of SUNSPOTS")

# demeaned series
ts2 = ts1-mean(ts1)
```

Part(b)
```{r}
# order p suggested by AIC
library(forecast)

auto.arima(ts2, max.p = 99, max.d = 0, max.q = 0, ic="aic", allowmean = FALSE)
```
AR(4) is suggested by AIC

```{r}
# order p suggested by BIC
auto.arima(ts2, max.p = 99, max.d = 0, max.q = 0, ic="bic", allowmean = FALSE)
```
AR(2) is suggested by BIC

```{r}
# order p suggested by PACF
par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 5.3, 2.1))
pacf(ts2, lag.max = 20, ylim=c(-1, 1))
```
AR(2) is suggested by PACF as PACF at h=2 is largest h that makes phi_hh_hat signifiacnt, other phi_hat are all within the significance band.

Part(c)
```{r}
# fit the time series by AR(2)
ar2 = arima(x=ts2, order=c(2, 0, 0), include.mean = FALSE, method = "ML")
ar2
```
Part(d)
```{r}
resid.ar2 = resid(ar2)

# plot the sample ACF and PACF of the residuals
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
par(mar = c(5.1, 4.1, 5.3, 2.1))
acf(resid.ar2, lag.max = 20, ylim = c(-1, 1))
pacf(resid.ar2, lag.max = 20, ylim = c(-1, 1))

# check the normal assumption of the residuals
qqnorm(resid.ar2, main = "")
qqline(resid.ar2)
```
From the above qq-norm plot, the sample points deviate from the qq-norm line at the two tails, so the model's residuals are NOT largely consistent with the assumption of normal distribution.

Part(e)

Denote X_t = SUNSPOTS at time t

X_t = 46.93 + Y_t with Y_t = 1.4064Y_t-1 - 0.7131Y_t-2 + Z_t, where Z_t is a white noise model.

```{r}
mean(ts1)
summary(ar2)
```
Part(f)

```{r}
t = 101:105
h = 5

# demeaned forecast
ts2.forecast = predict(ar2, h)

plus.or.minus = 1.96*ts2.forecast$se

# mean
mean.forecast = mean(ts1)

# combined forecast
ts.forecast.pred = mean.forecast + ts2.forecast$pred

lower = ts.forecast.pred - plus.or.minus
upper = ts.forecast.pred + plus.or.minus

# plot
plot(ts1, ylab="SUNSPOTS")
lines(t, ts.forecast.pred, lwd=2)
lines(t, lower, lty=2, lwd=2)
lines(t, upper, lty=2, lwd=2)
title("Forecasts for the SUNSPOTS time series")
```
